subject: Business Models
title: Managed vs Unmanaged Marketplaces
description: One-minute skill: Managed vs Unmanaged Marketplaces.

hook.text: Craigslist lets anyone post anything. Opendoor buys your house, fixes it, resells it. Same market, different control.

buildup.text: Unmanaged marketplaces connect parties and step back. Managed marketplaces control quality, pricing, or logistics.

discovery.text: Managed marketplaces have higher margins but lower scale. They trade growth speed for quality control.

twist.text: Amazon started as an unmanaged marketplace but now manages logistics (FBA), making it a hybrid.

climax.text: The trend is toward more management. Customers prefer guaranteed quality over unlimited choice.

punchline.text: Let anyone sell, or curate everything. Managed marketplaces are winning.

quiz.question: What defines a managed marketplace?
options: The platform controls quality, pricing, or logistics

details.summary: Managed marketplaces control the transaction experience end-to-end including pricing, quality standards, and fulfillment, while unmanaged marketplaces let buyers and sellers transact freely..
details.whyItMatters: The managed versus unmanaged choice determines a marketplace's unit economics, scalability, and user experience. Managed models like Opendoor in real estate trade scale for margin, while unmanaged models like Craigslist trade margin for reach.
takeaways: Managed marketplaces control pricing, quality, and fulfillment for consistent experiences
Unmanaged marketplaces provide tools but let participants transact independently
Managed models command higher take rates but face greater operational complexity

faq.question: What are examples of managed versus unmanaged marketplaces?
faq.answer: Managed: Uber sets prices and controls the ride experience. Opendoor buys and resells homes. StockX authenticates every sneaker. Unmanaged: eBay lets sellers set prices and ship directly. Craigslist provides listings with no transaction management. Facebook Marketplace facilitates connections only.

faq.question: How do you decide whether to build a managed or unmanaged marketplace?
faq.answer: Go managed when quality inconsistency kills trust, when the transaction is complex or high-stakes, or when controlling the experience creates significant value. Go unmanaged when the category is broad, transactions are simple, and users prefer flexibility over standardization.
